title: Tax audit
text: The tax authority has selected you for a full audit of the last three years.

out.text: They find errors. Honest ones, but errors.
They give up on most points.
The file is closed for lack of resources.
They estimate the bill themselves, generously.

lesson: Tax risk is a real liability even though it sits on no balance sheet. A good finance function is cheaper than a bad audit.

title: They have found the structure
text: Tax authorities in three countries are coordinating a challenge to your tax arrangements.

opts.label: Settle
opts.hint: Back taxes and a penalty, now.

opts.label: Fight it
opts.hint: Your advisers say the position is defensible.

out.text: You lose, with interest and penalties, in public.

lesson: The saving was a loan, and this is the repayment. Advisers are paid whether or not the scheme survives.

title: New data-privacy law
text: A sweeping privacy law takes effect next year. You hold a great deal of customer data.

opts.label: Do it properly
opts.hint: Rebuild data handling to meet the law in full.

out.text: Expensive, finished, and a selling point.

opts.label: Minimum compliance
opts.hint: A policy document and a cookie banner.

opts.label: Wait for enforcement
opts.hint: Nobody gets fined in the first year.

lesson: Compliance has a known cost; non-compliance has an unknown one with a fat tail. Regulators make examples of someone.

title: The regulator has noticed
text: You are the subject of a formal privacy investigation. The maximum fine is a percentage of global revenue.

opts.label: Pay and comply
opts.hint: Take the fine and fix it.

opts.label: Fight it
opts.hint: The law is new and untested.

out.text: You become the test case, and lose.

lesson: The cheap option was only cheap if nothing went wrong.

title: Minimum wage rises
text: The legal minimum is going up sharply. Even staff well above it will expect the difference to be kept.

opts.label: Just comply
opts.hint: Raise only those the law requires.

out.text: The lowest paid catch up with those above them.
Same cost, less output, unhappy people.

lesson: A wage floor compresses the whole pay scale. Labour-heavy, low-margin businesses feel it first.

title: A "facilitation payment"
text: An official in {city} has let it be known that your permit renewal would go faster with a contribution to his nephew’s consultancy.

out.text: The permit arrives on time anyway.
The permit arrives the next morning.
He is transferred. His colleagues process your file very carefully.

lesson: Small bribes are a trap: cheap today, and a permanent liability under laws that reach you wherever you are headquartered.

title: Bribery investigation
text: Prosecutors at home have opened a file on payments your company made to officials abroad.

out.text: A large fine and a monitor for three years.
The case is dropped for lack of evidence.

lesson: The payment was small. The liability never was.

title: The competition authority calls
text: Your share in {city} has attracted an inquiry into whether you are abusing a dominant position.

out.text: A year of document requests, then a clean bill.

opts.label: Offer remedies
opts.hint: Cut prices 5% to make it go away.

out.text: A fine, and a consent decree.

lesson: Past a certain share, growth itself becomes a regulatory risk. Dominance is a privilege with conditions.

title: Sustainability reporting is now mandatory
text: Companies your size must publish audited figures on emissions, pay gaps and supply chains.

out.text: The first report is unflattering and credible.

lesson: Disclosure turns reputation into something measurable — and makes gaming it a risk with a paper trail.

title: Your sustainability claims fall apart
text: An investigative piece has compared your sustainability report with your actual operations.

out.text: Trust will take years to rebuild.

lesson: A reputation built on claims is a liability waiting for a fact-checker.

title: Are your contractors employees?
text: New rules in {region} say long-term contractors must be offered employment, with benefits.

out.text: You keep things as they are.

lesson: Flexible labour is cheaper until a court decides it was employment all along.

title: Back pay ordered
text: A tribunal has ruled that your contractors were employees. Back pay, benefits and penalties are due.

opts.label: Pay
opts.hint: There is no appeal worth making.

lesson: The saving was real, and so was the liability accruing alongside it.

title: R&D tax credit
text: The government has introduced a generous credit for research spending.

opts.label: Maximise it
opts.hint: Reclassify as much spending as possible as research.

out.text: You leave the money on the table.

lesson: Subsidies change the after-tax cost of an activity. Use them — but aggressive claims invite the audit that reviews everything else too.

title: A new licence requirement
text: From next quarter, operating in {city} requires a licence that takes months to obtain.
lesson: Regulation is a fixed cost of market entry. Incumbents with compliance teams barely notice; newcomers pay full price.

title: Shut down for inspection
text: Inspectors have closed part of your {city} operation for trading without a licence.

out.text: A fine, a closure, and the licence you should have had.

lesson: Patchy enforcement is still enforcement.

title: Surprise inspection
text: Health inspectors have arrived unannounced at your {city} location.

out.text: A list of violations and a fine.

opts.label: Ask them to come back
opts.hint: Buy a week to tidy up.

out.text: They return suspicious, and look harder.

lesson: Standards you keep only for inspectors are not standards. A quality system turns inspections into non-events.

title: The safety regulator visits
text: Following the accident, the safety regulator has inspected every plant you run.

out.text: A fine and an expensive list of fixes.

lesson: Regulators follow accidents. Systemic problems get systemic inspections.

title: Subsidy repeal
text: The government in {region} has announced it will end feed-in support for new renewable projects next year.

opts.label: Rush projects in before the deadline
Adapt
opts.hint: Projects that only work with subsidies should not be built.

lesson: Policy-dependent returns carry political risk. The best projects still make sense when the subsidy goes away.

title: Stuck in the connection queue
text: Your next project is ready to connect, but the grid operator says the queue is two years long.

out.text: You skip the queue at a price.

lesson: Infrastructure bottlenecks, not technology, decide how fast clean energy gets built.

title: Conflict of interest
text: You are advising two companies that have just announced they are bidding for the same target.

opts.label: Resign one client
opts.hint: Keep the bigger one, explain to the other.

out.text: It does not, and it becomes a story.

lesson: In advisory work reputation is the asset. Conflicts that look manageable inside the firm look different on a front page.

title: Fast-track designation
text: The regulator has granted your lead programme a fast-track designation for an unmet medical need.

opts.label: Bank the news
opts.hint: Announce it and raise money on it.

lesson: Regulatory designations change the odds and the timeline. Markets price both immediately.
